I use an about a 5 year old Toshiba laptop with a dual core AMD64 CPU. I use Studio One with various VSTs and Kontakt 5. The main thing I have to deal with is the CPU "redlining" and cutting out (like a Youtube video playing that isn't buffering properly) my audio when using various Kontakt multis, also cutting out after adding over six or so tracks. Now, bouncing the raw data to audio is helpful in reducing cutout, but using various effect plugins as well, for example, for mixing and mastering, and you quickly use up the computers capabilities. What you are needing is the best bang for your buck as far as processing power. I would stay away from laptops with AMD CPUs. Try getting one with an Intel Core series, such as the i3, i5, I believe that Reason can be configured to support multicores as well.
